MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer on MLB's proposal that would overhaul the offseason calendar and shrink most of free agency to a short window in December:

"The league, through their propaganda arm, is promoting their latest set of roster and transaction proposals as player-friendly. 

"MLB expressly conditioned these proposals on the players’ agreement to a salary cap system, which would drastically reduce overall player compensation, eliminate fully guaranteed contracts through escrow, and turn back the clock on fundamental player rights.

"Their latest proposals regarding free agency would eliminate Player rights by establishing an artificial free agency window, subject to a salary cap, which would reduce player leverage and create a game of musical chairs pitting player vs. player. 

"The suggestion that the only way to limit roster churn, or incentivize earlier Free Agent signings is with a salary cap is entirely unserious. Players have proposed changes that would address these priorities, but the league is not interested in any changes that don’t directly reduce the rights of all players and shift leverage to the owners."

Major League Baseball today proposed drastic changes to its offseason calendar, including shortening free agency to a two- to three-week window every offseason, sources tell ESPN. The details of the proposal:

- A free agent dead period until the first day of the Winter Meetings in early December in which players and teams can negotiate but no deals can be signed. Trades would be allowed during this period
- Free agency would open the Monday the Winter Meetings begin and would close Dec. 21.
- From Dec. 21 through the first Monday in February, no free agent signings or trades would be allowed
- Free agents could sign and trades would be allowed again from the first Monday in February onward

Betting on yourself can change your career…

But sometimes, it can cost you MILLIONS 😳

From Caleb Martin passing on Miami’s long-term money before eventually signing a smaller deal with Philadelphia, to Jonathan Kuminga landing only $12.4 million with Minnesota after previously having a much larger Warriors offer on the table, this list is full of brutal contract decisions.

But No. 1 belongs to James Harden.

The Nets offered Harden a 3-year, $161 million extension in 2021, and after years of contract twists, the missed opportunity ultimately cost him upward of $60 million compared with that deal 👀

Sometimes betting on yourself pays off.

Sometimes it becomes one of the biggest bag fumbles in NBA history 😬

Steph Curry has been the NBA’s highest-paid player for 10 straight seasons 💰

The last time someone else held the top spot was 2016-17, when LeBron James led the league. Curry was coming off back-to-back MVP seasons and making just $12.1 million in the final year of his four-year, $44 million extension.

Then everything changed.

In 2017-18, Curry jumped to $34.7 million and took over as the NBA’s highest-paid player. He hasn’t given up that spot since 👀

Now, heading into 2026-27, Curry is still No. 1 at 38 years old, set to make $62.6 million 💰

Ten straight seasons at the top, and there could be another massive payday coming.

when will Fernando Mendoza be ready to start?

a deep dive into the metrics, the situation, the history of other No. 1 overall drafted QBs and what the Raiders are likely to do:

https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/analysis/fernando-mendoza-preseason-stats/

none of this is a knock on Mendoza, the coaching staff's development of him or where the Raiders drafted him

none of this matters for his long term upside after he has a chance to develop further

in fact, it's why the Raiders were extremely smart to sign a QB like Cousins in free agency to let Mendoza develop

but he's not ready

this is why HC Klint Kubiak said after Mendoza's third preseason game:

"He needs another  three preseason games... 

And now that the season's starting, the practice reps get smaller, and that's just life."

interesting added bit of context:

the solution is NOT to tell Mendoza to throw the ball away more

he already has a 13.3% throwaway rate

#1 of any QB this preseason

2025 reg season, the QB avg throwaway rate was 4.6% 

highest was 11.8% (Russell Wilson)

NFL average pressure/hit rates on blitzes:

this preseason: 36% pressure rate, 16% hit rate
2025 reg season: 43% pressure rate, 20% hit rate
---
Mendoza to-date: 70% pressure rate, 50% hit rate

Raiders QB blitz, pressure & hit numbers:

Cousins: 4 blitzes, 0 pressures/hits (0%)
O'Connell: 9 blitzes, 4 pressures (44%), 1 hit (11%)
Mendoza: 10 blitzes, 7 pressures (70%), 5 hits (50%)

these Mendoza numbers are untenable

you can't operate an offense AND your QB will get hurt

Mendoza's time to throw is well above average

and while some starting QBs are in that ballpark (Lamar Jackson and even Brock Purdy), they hold the ball to push it downfield:

% of att beyond the sticks:

39% Purdy
38% Lamar
18% Mendoza

last NFL season, the lowest % of att beyond the sticks for any QB was 24%

but those numbers aren't the biggest red flags for Fernando Mendoza

these are:

70% of blitzes recorded pressure (#59)

37% pressure rate (#51)

only 18% of attempts went beyond the sticks (#60)

3.0 sec time to throw (#58)

before we dive into the most concerning stats, let's talk standard passing metrics:

Mendoza, out of 63 qualifying QBs right now:

#55 in EPA/att (-0.36)
#45 in YPA (5.3)
#55 net yds/att (4.5)
#52 in comp rate (55.6%)
#51 in passer rating (59.5)

keep in mind, most of the competition (min 20 dropbacks) are second, third and fourth string QBs who will never start in the NFL

yes, he's playing with backups - but yes, he's playing defensive backups, often not just second but third string defenders

alarming final preseason stats from Fernando Mendoza

51 dropbacks... with only 25 completions

14 hits taken, #1 most in NFL

29% hit rate, #2 highest in NFL
